title: Dieting But Weight Not Dropping: 7 Common Reasons
intro: If you feel you've been watching what you eat but the scale won't budge, you're not alone. Usually there are a few small things being overlooked, and most of them can be fixed.

sections.h: Reasons 1 & 2: Hidden calories and too much 'healthy' food
sections.p: Lots of curry kuah poured on, cooking oil, sambal, teh tarik and packet drinks all have calories, but they're rarely counted. 'Healthy' foods like oats with honey, nuts, dried fruit and wholemeal bread still have calories if the portion is big. Healthy doesn't always mean low calorie.

sections.h: Reason 3: Weekends undo your weekday effort
sections.p: Monday to Friday you watch your food, but Saturday and Sunday there are kenduri, family meals and brunch. These two days alone can cancel out the deficit you built all week. You don't need to avoid every event, just plan a little.

sections.h: Reason 4: Water weight and your menstrual cycle
sections.p: Weight can go up 1 to 2 kg within a day or two because of water, salty food or before your period. This is not fat. That's why weighing every day without looking at the average can make you feel like you've failed, even when you're actually making progress.

sections.h: Reasons 5 & 6: Poor sleep, stress and not enough protein
sections.p: Not enough sleep and high stress make your appetite harder to control. If there's little protein in your meals, you get hungry again quickly and it's harder to keep your muscle. Try to have a protein source at every meal, like eggs, chicken, fish, tauhu or tempe.

sections.h: Reason 7: So strict you can't keep it up
sections.p: A diet that's too little usually only lasts 1 to 2 weeks before you go off track. A moderate plan you can repeat every week works better. If you've been consistent for months and still see no change, see a doctor to check for conditions like thyroid problems or PCOS.

action: Record everything you eat and drink for 3 days, including sweet drinks and kuah.
Weigh yourself in the morning, then calculate the weekly average and compare week to week.
Add one protein source to every meal, for example eggs, chicken, fish or tauhu.
For weekends, plan one free meal, not one free day.
myth: Many think their weight won't drop because their metabolism is 'broken'. In fact, the cause is usually food estimates that are off and changes in water weight. Metabolism does slow down a little as weight drops, but it is not 'broken'.

faq.q: How long should I wait before changing my plan?
faq.a: Give it 2 to 4 weeks and look at the trend in your average weight and waist measurement. One week is too short to draw a conclusion, especially if that week is close to your period.

faq.q: Do I need to eat even less?
faq.a: Check your food record first. Usually the problem is hidden calories or weekends, not that you need to cut even more food.

faq.q: I've done everything, but it's still not dropping. Why?
faq.a: Conditions like thyroid problems, PCOS or certain medications can affect weight. See a doctor for a check-up before you cut your food more strictly.
